Q: Should a C++ logger write method be defined as const? A:

I'd say it should NOT be const. Writing to the logger changes some state of (or some state associated with) the logger - and that state is presumably meaningful to the user of the class.

In your example, Logger::Write() changes the value of a message counter. That change of value is, logically, a change of state of the Logger - its value is meaningful to the user of the class.

mutable has its uses. But using it to work around a need for a const member function to change meaningful state of an object is not one of them.

Q: Error : Message has reached MaxDequeueCount of 5. Moving message to queue 'webjobs-blobtrigger-poison' A:

Maybe not the solution for this question, but I struggled with this problem for several hours. Queue messages went straight to the poison queue with a “MaxDequeueCount of 5”, even though I had set maxDequeueCount: 3 in host.json.

What fooled me was this: the error message said “5”, but my configuration said “3”. It took a while before I realized that this was actually a hint.

Solution: Check what is actually present in the output folder:

Get-Content "bin\Debug\net8.0\host.json"

Mine showed "isDefaultHostConfig": true — meaning it was an auto-generated default file, not my own configuration!

Fix: Clean + Rebuild. The problem was that PreserveNewest in the .csproj did not overwrite the existing file. After running dotnet clean && dotnet build, my host.json was copied correctly and everything worked.

Tip: Use <CopyToOutputDirectory>Always</CopyToOutputDirectory> instead of PreserveNewest to avoid this in the future.

Hope it can help some other having this problem.

Q: What exactly does AI do beyond ML models and rule-based logic? A:

Up to about the 2022 launch of ChatGPT, AI referred to academic research in several areas (control systems, cybernetics, symbolic reasoning, knowledge bases, PCA, bayesian reasoning and networks, markov chains, ANNs, and more), with a modern history going back to the 1940s or 1950s, sometimes dated very specifically to the 1956 Dartmouth conference, and a kind of pre-history in clockwork, calculators, and the analytical engine.

But “AI” is now a marketing term. The buzzword usage is the meaning. Whereas, machine learning is still a somewhat well-defined academic subject area, at the crossover of computing and statistics.

So now it means whatever the current commercial state of the art is for products that can be successfully marketed with that label, and this is a fast-moving target!

Three years ago, a pure LLM could be marketed as AI, but agentic AI, the use of MCP servers, and, as you say, rule-based logic have all been gathered under the umbrella term. What AI means in two years time will likely depend on what research and breakthroughs (whether in ML or other fields, for instance cybernetics or symbolic reasoning) occur.

Perhaps it could once more refer to the academic discipline, but once a term has reached popular culture, it largely means what non-specialists think it means.

Q: How do you know system app for given extension? A:

File extensions are arbitrarily assigned by developers. I am not aware of a central registry. Thus, it is possible for entirely independent developers to adopt a common file extension even though the file contents may have no compatibility.

That said, this problem has been avoided for common software packages. You can find a long list of extensions in current or past usage at [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_file_formats].

Turning to your specific question about OpenOffice and LibreOffice, the packages share some development history, but OpenOffice has now largely been abandoned. As a result, the package that opens the file is the one that is installed on the computer that is trying to open it. Both will also open .XLSX and .DOCX files, with varying degrees of compatibility, even though that's a Microsoft format.

.CSV files can be opened by many packages with varying results. Any given machine may have multiple programs that can open them.The one you use depends on what you're trying to achieve.

The upshot of all this is that you'll probably have to examine the host machine to find out what is installed in order to answer the question. This is not straightforward in Windows. Linux has its own complications

Q: MongoDB Atlas connection fails with querySrv ECONNREFUSED from Node.js A:

When this happened to me, I managed to solve it by changing the connection string format.

It should be an SRV lookup failure.

Try changing the connection string, look it up on Atlas and use this format:

mongodb://<username>:<password>
